title: Cap. III Sol. Rat. 13: nearer point — gratuitous election stabilizes hortations as ordained media
pass_a_gloss: But nearer to the matter, I say that by this doctrine of gratuitous election hortations and corrections are stabilized, and men's wills are kindled to living piously; because we so preach the secret will of God concerning electing certain men, that at the same time we do not keep silent about his revealed will, which has decreed that these elect are to be led to the end destined for them only through means ordained by God. But hortations, corrections, prayers, and things of that kind are held by all among those means which the Divine wisdom has ordained for promoting the elect's salvation.
pass_b_english: Nearer the point: I say this doctrine of gratuitous election stabilizes hortations and corrections and kindles men's wills to live piously — because we preach God's secret will to elect certain persons without silencing his revealed will, which decrees those elect are led to their destined end only through means God ordained. Hortations, corrections, prayers, and the like are among those means Divine wisdom ordained to promote the elect's salvation.
source_text: Sed propius ad rem, Dico, hac doctrina gratuitae electionis stabiliri hortationes et correptiones, incendi hominum voluntates ad pie vivendum; quia sic arcanam Dei de eligendis certis hominibus voluntatem praedicamus, ut simul revelatam ejus voluntatem non taceamus, quae hosce electos non nisi per media a Deo ordinata ad finem illis destinatum perducendos decrevit. Hortationes autem, correptiones, orationes, et id genus alia, ab omnibus habentur inter illa media, quae promovendae electorum saluti Divina sapientia ordinavit.
